absent: Enabled tracing backend behavior for lifecycle, snapshot and print helpers beyond the inert placeholders is not shown.
Real formatting, overflow handling and user copy semantics of formatted output when enabled are not shown.
Concrete definitions of sequence wrapper, filesystem node, path, file, module, notifier, read copy update primitives and static call mechanics are not shown.
Probe priority ordering, taint policy, notifier chains and module iteration order are not shown.
Task recursion field width, tracepoint object layout offsets and section placement details beyond named constants are not shown.
Remote buffer lifecycle, field metadata layout and packet filter invocation are not shown.

findings.text: In the configuration captured here, global tracing lifecycle operations have no effect. Requesting start, stop, on, off, snapshot or snapshot allocation leaves state unchanged, stack dump requests are ignored, and the query for whether tracing is active reports inactive.
Print style tracing helpers in this configuration discard their inputs and report zero, indicating no bytes recorded and no error. The dump mode selector is accepted but causes no action.

Per task recursion state is a bitset partitioned into families. One family tracks function tracing, a second tracks internal tracing, a third tracks internal event tracing, each with separate slots for normal, interrupt, soft interrupt, nonmaskable and transition execution. Additional independent slots cover branch handling, interrupt graph handling reused from existing state, and protection of the recording path itself. Small helpers set, clear and test a single slot in the current task state.

Recursion context geometry uses 4 bits per family. The function family begins at the first function slot, the internal family at the first internal slot, and the event family at the first internal event slot. The context mask denotes the low portion up to the internal start plus the width.

Execution contexts are distinguished into five abstract levels covering nonmaskable, hard interrupt, soft interrupt, normal and transition. The current level is derived from the platform interrupt level by counting down from normal, so deeper hardware contexts map to earlier abstract codes.

Recording guard has two builds. One build checks the dedicated recording slot and, only when free, briefly claims it around the recording call to suppress reentry. The other build performs no recording and no guard manipulation.

Read copy update observation check has two builds. One build reports whether observation is inactive and, when inactive and the recording guard is free, emits a single warning naming the offending address before releasing the guard. The other build unconditionally reports observation as healthy.

Recursion admission is a claim and release protocol keyed by execution context plus family base. A claimant provides addresses and a family base and either receives ownership of one slot or receives a failure indication. Ownership is exclusive per context except that a single transition overlap is tolerated to avoid dropping events when interrupt state lags; a second overlap fails and triggers the recording guard. Release returns the slot to free. Only a successful claim may be released.

A successful claim holds non tracing preemption disabled across the critical section, with an ordering barrier between flag update and preemption change. Release restores non tracing preemption before clearing the flag, again separated by ordering. The function tracing convenience wrappers use the function family base for both claim and release.

Remote tracing backend is described by a table of seven operations: initialization with filesystem node and private data, loading a buffer descriptor for a size, unloading a descriptor, toggling tracing, swapping a per cpu reader page, resetting per cpu state, and toggling an event by numeric identity. Each operation carries opaque private data and reports status where applicable.

Remote event transport groups a minimal header carrying numeric identity with a richer descriptor. The descriptor holds a fixed length name store, numeric identity, enabled flag, back pointer to remote state, pointer to field metadata, format string, and print callback receiving event memory and sequence state. Helper macros declare typed payload members, pass through member lists, and define a per name format type that prefixes caller payload with the header.
Remote event names allow up to 30 bytes in the fixed store.
Formatted trace output uses a total capacity of 8192 bytes. Usable payload is that total minus the combined footprint of the embedded sequence wrapper, the read offset and the full indicator.
Formatted output state combines an embedded sequence wrapper with a read offset, a full indicator and an inline byte store sized to the usable payload.

Initialization binds the embedded wrapper to the inline store and clears full and offset state. Usage queries expose used length, a write pointer at the end of used data, an overflow predicate that is true when either the full indicator or the wrapper overflow is set, and a pop operation that discards the most recent unit.

In the configuration shown, higher level formatting and sink operations are inert. Character, string, memory, hexadecimal, bitmask and path appends accept inputs without effect, sequence to file and sequence to user transfers report zero, and buffer acquisition for a length reports absence.

Event filesystem entries pair a name with a lookup callback and a release callback. Lookup receives the name plus mode and data out parameters and reports status; release receives the name and stored data without return.

Flag printing pairs a mask with a name for both native width and sixty four bit masks. Probe registration entries hold a function pointer, opaque data and priority. Extension blocks hold registration and unregistration hooks plus a single faultable bit. The tracepoint object itself groups a name, a disabled by default branch key, static call key and trampoline, iterator and stub pointers, a protected array of probe entries, and an optional extension pointer.
Tracepoint pointer indirection has two builds. One build represents a reference as a constant integer offset; the other represents it as a constant direct pointer.
The bridge to packet filter programs groups a tracepoint pointer with a program pointer, an argument count and a writable size, with overall alignment to 32 bytes.
Declaration exposes an external tracepoint object per logical name. The enabled query is a rarely taken branch on the object key in the enabled build and a constant false in the disabled build.
Evaluation mapping entries associate a subsystem name and expression text with a numeric value.
Probes registered without explicit priority use priority 10.
Registration that tolerates preexisting entries forwards to the priority aware variant using the default priority.
Module tracking nodes link through a list head and retain a pointer to the owning module.

In the configuration shown, module taint evaluation always reports clean, module notifier registration and unregistration report success without effect, and iteration over module tracepoints performs no callbacks.

Unregistration synchronization has two builds. The active build waits for both tasks trace grace and tracepoint sleepable grace; deferred release uses sleepable grace for atomic context and tasks trace for syscall context. The inert build performs no waiting and no deferred invocation.
Faultability is determined by presence of an extension marked faultable in the active build and is unconditionally non faultable in the inert build.

Several helpers are pure syntactic pass through or empty markers: parameter list wrappers forward their arguments unchanged, enumeration and size helpers expand to nothing, and the global enabled marker carries no value.

Pointer resolution has two builds matching the pointer representation: offset arithmetic versus direct load. Registration of the tracepoint address into the dedicated section likewise has two builds: one emits a relative reference with alignment via assembly, the other defines a used static pointer variable placed in that section.

Probe dispatch has two builds. One loads the probe array without protection checks and, when non empty, invokes the static call target with the first entry data and caller arguments. The other invokes the generated iterator directly with null data and caller arguments.
Language bridge macros include an empty placeholder and a generator that defines a non traced function per event which forwards its parameters to the corresponding internal trace implementation.
A check helper records the event name as a used string in a dedicated verification section.

Declaration generators provide a uniform per event interface: registration, priority registration, unregistration, callback type checking, and two enabled queries with the public one adding a lock aware observation warning. The plain event implementation guards dispatch with a fast sleepable guard under a caller condition and only runs when the branch key is active; the syscall implementation instead guards with tasks trace protection, permits faults, and does not test a caller condition.

Definition generators instantiate per event storage: a name string in its section, an iterator that walks the probe array to its terminator invoking each entry with its data, an empty stub, a tracepoint object initialized with name, disabled key, static call linkage, iterator and stub pointers, empty probe list and supplied extension, plus static call and language bridge definitions. Convenience forms supply an extension with caller hooks and non faultable marking, a faultable marking for syscalls, or no extension. Export forms publish the tracepoint object, iterator and static call linkage as general or restricted symbols while also recording the check entry.

Callers of the recursion claim must treat negative return as dropped event with no ownership acquired; only non negative returns convey a slot that must later be released exactly once. Reentry in the same context without transition room, or observation inactive, leads to loss rather than blocking.

Callers must not assume disabled formatting helpers transfer data: user copy and file print report zero processed, path handling reports zero, and direct buffer acquisition reports absence, so output must be treated as discarded.
Headers use single definition guards to ensure single inclusion.
